THESE APPEALS ALONG WITH MFA CROBs, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
In respect of the accident which occurred on 21.06.2015, two claim petitions were filed seeking compensation for the death of Susheelamma, a 53 years old and the death of Harshitha, a 16 year old.
Two claim petitions were filed by their legal representatives.
2. In respect of injuries, a claim petition was filed by the injured.

3. The Tribunal has record a finding that an accident did occur which had resulted in two deaths and injuries also were suffered by the claimant and has proceeded to award a sum of Rs.10,95,000/-,
Rs.5,16,857/- and Rs.3,93,408/-.

Being aggrieved - 10 - The Manager vs Jyothi on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85781758/
8 NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS by these awards, both insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal.
4. The insurer contends that the Tribunal could not have fastened liability on it, especially when there were three people being carried in a motorcycle.
It is also sought to be contended that the quantum of compensation awarded was on the higher side.
5. The claimants on the other hand contend that the sums awarded are inadequate and they are required to be enhanced.
6. The Tribunal has record a finding that an accident did occur between the car and the motorcycle which had resulted in two deaths and one injury.
The Police after investigation have laid a charge sheet against the driver of the car.
The driver of the car has not been examined to establish that there was any negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS

7. It is settled law that merely because three people are being carried in a motorcycle (Mohammed Siddique's case1) an inference cannot be drawn that there was negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
8. In that view the matter, there is no merit in the appeal of the insurer and the same is accordingly dismissed.

9. As far as the quantum of competition is concerned, it is noticed that for death of Susheelamma,
the Tribunal has taken the notional income of Rs.9,000/- per month, which is in accordance with the sum determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and hence it is accepted.
It is however noticed that the Tribunal has not added the future prospects of 10%.

Consequently, in respect of the death of Susheelamma, the notional income would Mohammed Siddique v. National Insurance Company Ltd. - AIR 2020 SC 520 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS be taken at Rs.9,900/- {Rs.9,000/- + Rs.900/- (10%)} and since she had husband and three children, 1/4th would have to be deducted towards her personal expenses and, as a consequence, she would be entitled to Rs.9,80,100/- (Rs.9,900/- - Rs.2,475/-
(1/4th) = Rs.7,425/- X 12 X 11) towards 'loss of dependency'.

sentences.text: 10. The claimants being the husband and also the children, each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/-, it would be Rs.1,93,600/- (Rs.48,400/- X 4 members) towards 'loss of love and affection' apart from Rs.36,300/- under the 'conventional heads'.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has also awarded a sum of Rs.1,78,000/- towards 'medical expenses'.
In my view, it is based on the documentary evidence and is therefore affirmed.
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS 12.

Consequently, the legal representatives of the deceased Susheelamma in MFA No.8908/2017 would be entitled to a compensation of Rs.13,88,000/- as against Rs.10,95,000/- awarded by the Tribunal along with a rate of 6% interest per annum from the date of petition till its reliasation.
13. However, the legal representatives of deceased Susheelamma in MFA No.8908/2017 would not be entitled for interest for the delayed period as per order dated 01.02.2021.
14. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

15. As far as the death of a 16 year old - Harshitha is concerned, this Court in MFA.11440/2011 c/w.
MFA.206/2018 has laid down guidelines for payment - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS of compensation to the parents of a minor who was killed in an accident.

16. As per the said judgment, since the accident was of the year 2015 (as per Table - 3.4 of the said judgment), the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.13,27,090/- as compensation along with a sum of Rs.16,857/- towards 'medical expenses' of the deceased.
Hence, the claimants would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.13,43,947/-.
17. The said sums shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of payment.
18. This sum shall be invested in a 'Cumulative Fixed Deposit' in a Nationalised bank of the choice of the parents till one of them reaches the age of 60 years.
The accumulated amount shall be paid to them thereafter.
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS 19.

It is made clear that it will be open for the parents to approach the Tribunal and seek partial or complete withdrawal of the accumulated sum at any point in time by producing material or attendant circumstances which would satisfy the Tribunal that there is an overwhelming need of The Manager vs Jyothi on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85781758/
10 money for the parents.

20. The insurer shall also issue a Medical Insurance Policy in the name of the parents to the extent of Rs.10 lakhs, which would come into effect from the date on which one of the parent attain the age of 60 years.
An option to purchase an additional cover by the parents, at their own cost (popularly termed as "Top-up Cover" by the insurers), shall also be provided.
21. As far as injuries is concerned, it is noticed that the claimant had suffered a fracture of the femur and tibia.
The doctor who was examined has assessed the whole body disability at 35% to the left lower - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS limb and 30% to the right lower limb.
The doctor has not assessed the whole body disability.
In my view, since the claimant has suffered a fracture of the left femur and the tibia, it would be appropriate to treat the whole world disability at 15%.
22. The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.6,000/- per month, since there was no proof of actual income.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income at Rs.9,000/- for the accident of the year 2015, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/-.

Consequently, towards 'loss of future earnings' the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,26,800/- (Rs.9,000/- X 12 X 14 X 15%)
23.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view, it would be - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:50881 AND 3 OTHERS appropriate to enhance the said sums to Rs.70,000/- and Rs.60,000/- respectively.

24. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.99,368/-
awarded towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.30,000/- towards 'future medical expenses' which are based on documentary evidence and are affirmed.
25. A sum of Rs.25,000/- awarded towards 'food, nutrition, conveyance and attendant charges' is also affirmed.
26. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as three months.

In my view, it would be appropriate to treat the laid up period as four months and award a sum of Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000/- X 4 months)
towards 'loss of earning during laid up period'.
